exposure: diastolic blood pressure at admission (>110 mmHg vs. <110 mmHg)
cohort: The study included 241 preeclamptic patients whose medical files were reviewed after they were admitted and delivered in Woldia General Hospital between 2011 and 2016.
finding: Maternal diastolic blood pressure greater than 110 mmHg at admission was significantly associated with nearly 3 times higher perinatal death compared to women with diastolic blood pressures below 110 mmHg.
